scenes.headline: Data Masking
scenes.subtitle: Hide sensitive values without copying data
scenes.narration: Data masking obscures sensitive column values at query time so users see only what they are permitted to.

scenes.headline: What masking protects
items: PII like SSNs, emails, and phone numbers
scenes.narration: Masking guards personally identifiable information from casual exposure. It protects regulated financial and health data. In short, it covers any field where full visibility is a compliance risk.

scenes.headline: A column mask in Unity Catalog
scenes.code:
-- Define a masking function
CREATE FUNCTION main.security.mask_ssn(ssn STRING)
RETURN CASE
  WHEN is_account_group_member('pii_readers') THEN ssn
  ELSE 'XXX-XX-' || substr(ssn, -4)
END;

-- Attach it to a column
ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees
  ALTER COLUMN ssn SET MASK main.security.mask_ssn;
scenes.narration: We define a UDF that returns the full SSN only to members of a privileged group. Everyone else sees the last four digits with the rest masked. Attaching it as a column mask enforces the rule automatically on every query.

scenes.headline: Static vs dynamic masking

columns.title: Dynamic
points: Masked at query time by role

scenes.narration: Static masking writes an already-masked copy, useful for test environments. Dynamic masking keeps the original data and applies masks per user at query time. Unity Catalog column masks are dynamic, so one table serves all audiences.

scenes.headline: Best practices
items: Base masks on group membership, not individuals
Combine with row-level filters for full coverage
scenes.narration: Drive masking decisions from groups so policies stay maintainable. Shared masking functions keep logic consistent across tables. Pairing masks with row filters protects both columns and rows together.

scenes.text: Mask sensitive columns dynamically so the right people see the right detail.
scenes.narration: One governed table can safely serve analysts, auditors, and the public alike.
